6415798093069021093:
They say there are three hardest trades under heaven: boating, blacksmithing, and making tofu.
Hu Sanli remembered when his father was still around, every afternoon around 1 PM, he would start preparing tofu for the next day. Good tofu requires ten meticulous steps. First, one must pick the plumpest soybeans from a large batch. His father was the most honest man—never using spoiled beans to cut corners. After his father’s careful selection, only a small portion would remain in the basket. These chosen beans would then soak in cold spring water fetched at dawn for over ten hours before anyone could rest.
By midnight, when everyone else was asleep, Hu Sanli would hear his father rise to grind the beans. Timing was everything—miss it, and the tofu wouldn’t taste right. Back then, grinding a basin of beans took six hours.
At twenty, Hu Sanli wiped the sweat from his brow, panting. This was his second batch of tofu tonight. He recalled his father making four batches in a single night, yet now, he could barely manage two. Where exactly did his skills fall short compared to his father’s?
